points.description: States that a function signature includes the name of the function (the function name/identifier).
States that it includes the types of the parameters (the parameter type list, i.e. data types of the arguments), using correct terms such as 'parameter types'.
points.partial_credit: Half: mentions parameters but without their types (e.g. 'the parameters' or 'number of parameters' only).

points.description: Gives both elements together as the signature's content, with no wrong extra element (e.g. does not claim the signature includes the function body or the parameter names as required parts).

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the function name and the parameter types, stated precisely. Saying only 'parameters' without types earns at most half of P2; naming only one element earns just that point. Any wrong inclusion, such as the function body, loses P3, and vague statements like 'details about the function' earn nothing. A return type is not in the model answer, so mentioning it neither earns nor costs marks unless it replaces a required element.
